title: Level 2 Chemistry: Properties of Selected Organic Compounds -- 2024
subject: chemistry

questions.text:
The leaves of kawakawa have been used to treat a range of conditions, including toothache and gastrointestinal upsets. Recent research has shown medicinal effects can be attributed to many molecules in kawakawa, including vitexin.

[Diagram shows vitexin molecule with two functional groups A and B circled. Group A is shown as an aldehyde/carbonyl group (H-C=O-H). Group B is shown as an alkene (C=C with H atoms).]

questions.text:
Kawakawa also contains some anti-inflammatory molecules. When researchers extracted these molecules from kawakawa leaves, they had to use a range of solvents including methanol, ethanol, and hexane. All three of these solvents are colourless liquids at room temperature.

Explain the procedure you could use to distinguish between methanol, ethanol, and hexane, based solely on their physical properties.

Give reasons for the different results between solvents.

Physical properties are limited to differences in melting point, boiling point, and solubility in water.
questions.expectedAnswer: Mix each unknown solvent in a test tube with water.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies ethanol or methanol as miscible/soluble OR identifies hexane as an alkane. Merit: Correctly identifies hexane as non-soluble AND provides method to distinguish between alcohols. Excellence: Explains how all three can be distinguished, with reference to solubility, molecular structure, and carbon chain effects.

questions.text:
Polystyrene has been used widely in the manufacture of plastic produce such as bags, plates, bowls, and cutlery. However, single-use plastics, such as these, are being phased out.

Polystyrene is an addition polymer made from the styrene monomer.

[Diagram shows styrene monomer: a benzene ring attached to C=C with H atoms]

In the box below, draw three repeating units of the polystyrene polymer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Three repeating units showing the C-C backbone (no double bonds) with alternating benzene ring...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies polymer is orientated correctly (C-C unsaturated). Merit: Labels saturated (C-C) or monomer is unsaturated (C=C).

questions.text:
Plastics are cheap and stable.

Explain why the monomer styrene is more reactive than the polymer polystyrene.

In your answer you should:
- explain the term 'addition polymerisation'
- explain the difference in structure, and link it to chemical reactivity
- relate how this difference is important for the uses of the polymer.
questions.expectedAnswer: In an addition polymerisation reaction, C=C double bonds are broken to form single bonds,...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies polymer is orientated correctly OR partial explanation of addition polymerisation. Merit: Links saturated/unsaturated nature of polymer/monomer to materials reactivity AND explains addition polymerisation. Excellence: Explains the difference of monomer and polymer in terms of structure, reactivity and use.

questions.text:
The starting material Compound A, and one of the final products Compound G, are both secondary haloalkanes.

Draw the tertiary isomer of bromobutane and explain why it is classified as tertiary.
questions.expectedAnswer: Structure: (CH₃)₃C-Br (2-bromo-2-methylpropane). This is a tertiary haloalkane
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct structure OR explanation. Merit: Correct structure AND explanation.

questions.text:
When Compound B reacts with hydrochloric acid, HCl, without heat, two products are formed in differing amounts.

[Diagram shows Compound B: but-1-ene structure H₂C=CH-CH₂-CH₃]

Discuss the reaction of Compound B with hydrochloric acid.
In your answer you should:
- name and explain this type of reaction
- draw the structures of both products, in the appropriate box for the major and minor products
- justify your choice of major and minor products.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct structure for one product OR identifies the haloalkane is formed. Merit: Explains major/minor and identifies both structures. Excellence: Explanation of addition reaction, options for major/minor products, and why they are produced in this situation.

questions.text:

questions.text:
Compounds Q and R below each contain a carbon to carbon double bond, but only one of them can form geometric isomers.

H₂N-CH₂-CH=CH-CH₃     H₂N-CH₂-CH₂-CH=CH₂
     Compound Q                Compound R

Which compound forms geometric isomers?
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound Q will form geometric isomers.

questions.text: Draw the cis and trans geometric isomers that it forms in the boxes provided, and select the correct label.
questions.expectedAnswer: Trans isomer: NH₂CH₂ and CH₃ on opposite sides of the C=C double bond.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct compound and isomers identified. Merit: Both structures correct with correct cis/trans labels.
